Located close to both Broadway theatres and the Actors Studio training school, Hell's Kitchen has long been a home to learning and practicing actors.

Perched atop a bluff on a large corner lot abutting Atlantic Double Dunes Nature Preserve, this historical Bluff Road OCEAN-VIEW home epitomizes the authentic, understated, laid-back East End lifestyle that has captured artists and aesthetes for over a century. Just a short stroll to the village, Indian Wells Beach, and Atlantic Ave. Beach, this coveted property enjoys one of Amagansett’s best locations.

The interior of the main house (owned by the same family for four generations) is a perfect blend of charming original details and thoughtfully integrated modern amenities. Enjoy ocean breezes from the picturesque wrap-around front porch; dine alfresco on the elevated rear deck; bask in the sun from the expansive enclosed rear lawn (featuring free-form heated pool, Japanese-inspired landscaping, and flagstone patio); or enjoy the coveted “Hamptons light” from the home’s main living spaces – each of which feature multiple exposures and direct access to outdoor spaces.

Living room boasts original fireplace, wet bar, triple exposures (south, east, and west), and opens onto the home’s tour de force wrap-around front porch. Upgraded kitchen features multiple exposures, hand-hewn beam ceiling, stone counters, breakfast alcove, central butcher block island, and stainless steel appliances. Intimate formal dining room features hardwood flooring, wainscoting, and built-in china hutch (all original). Family room features triple exposures (north, south, and east), fireplace, built-in bookshelves, and flat screen tv. Both the dining and the family rooms feature French doors that open onto the elevated deck and expansive rear lawn beyond.

Upstairs, the master bedroom features sweeping ocean and dune views, multiple exposures, and en suite bathroom with double vanities and jetted soaking tub. Four well-proportioned sunny bedrooms complete the upstairs level.

Do not miss this wonderful opportunity to enjoy one of Amagansett’s most coveted properties.

This stately building is located in the heart of Manhattan’s Upper East Side, one of the most desirable neighborhoods in New York City. Hanley New York is within several blocks of the 4, 5, 6, N, Q and R subway lines and is a pleasant walk from Midtown and the Plaza District.

Inspired by the architecture of mid-century icons including Le Corbusier and Mies van der Rohe, and thoroughly updated for an effortlessly elevated 21st-century lifestyle, this property brings an unmistakably downtown edge to uptown living. The building’s original, namesake white glazed façade bricks – manufactured by Hanley Brick – are contrasted with new, black-glazed, subway-style bricks on accent walls throughout the ground level. Works of art by photographer Olaf Otto Becker and abstract painter Malcolm Hill are sophisticated complements to the Lobby by celebrated designers Enrico Bonetti and Shamir Shah. The amenities themselves are paired with white-glove services and tech-savvy features to offer residents every convenience along with a host of brilliantly contemporary luxuries.

The original, elegantly proportioned floor plans have been renovated with finishes and features that speak to modern tastes. In addition to hardwood floors throughout and upgraded kitchens, all residences will offer the comfort of thermostat-controlled HVAC. Select residences feature expansive terraces and balconies with extraordinary views of the New York City skyline as well as washer/dryers.

Modern design brilliance abounds in our well thought-out amenities. The concierge has ample storage for all of your deliveries including cold storage for groceries and flowers and hanging racks for laundry and dry cleaning in addition to shelving for standard packages that come for you. Our resident App alerts you in real time when your packages arrive and a digital message board in the mail room reminds you of your delivery upon arrival home. The Fitness Center, by Jay Wright of The Wright Fit, offers an innovative approach to health and wellness founded in the latest exercise science research. Overlooking the Courtyard, and designed with ample room to workout with your personal trainer, the Fitness Center is equipped with state-of-the-art exercise equipment including Woodway treadmills by 4Front and Cybex Arc Trainers. Inspired by the concept of an urban tree house, the expansive Resident Lounge has been designed with defined lounging and study areas as well as a children’s play space. description.41695: Beautifully Renovated 2 Bedroom, 1 Bath Residence in Brooklyn HeightsThese newly designed apartments give a nod to both the past and the present. Beautiful new finishes perfectly compliment Brooklyn Heights' old world feel, allowing one to transcend time.KitchensGorgeous Pickled Grey Hardwood FloorsPristine White CabinetsChevron Patterned BacksplashModern Chrome FaucetsBrand-new Washer Dryer in Every ResidenceFull size Stainless Steel Appliances with Bertazzoni StoveBathroomsState of the Art Chrome FinishesRecessed Niche Tub and Shower WallTastefully Arranged Snow White Subway Tile and Montauk Blue Slate TileToday, Brooklyn Heights is considered one of the most beautiful areas in Brooklyn. The neighborhood is known for its low rise architecture, 19th century brownstones, and cobble stoned, tree-lined streets. Stretching south from Old Fulton Street to Atlantic Avenue, and west from Cadman Plaza/Court Street to the Promenade and the East River, Brooklyn Heights in tucked in between DUMBO, Downtown Brooklyn, Cobble Hill and Boerum Hill. Main attractions of the community include Walt Whitman Park, the headquarters of the Brooklyn Historical Society and of course, the Brooklyn Heights Promenade. The Promenade overlooks the new Brooklyn Bridge Park, sweeping views of Downtown Manhattan, the Statue of Liberty, and is a central location for both locals and tourists alike to photograph the Manhattan Skyline, go for a jog, or just take in the scenery.Transportation is abound with the 2, 3, 4, 5, N, R, A, and C lines, as well as the East River Ferry. Moreover, whether you are looking for farm-to-table fare at Colonie, impeccable Italian at Sociale, or a simple tavern with fresh oysters and cold beer at Jack the Horse, there is certainly no shortage of delicious food and amazing culture. Brooklyn Heights continues to be a timeless neighborhood of Brooklyn and the exact reason why so many find it to be the perfect place to call home.Contact Sebastian for an exclusive viewing.** Advertised price is net effective of one month free at $4950/mo **

A rare opportunity to live in a newly revitalized rental building on the site of a former New York culinary "institution," where the city's most elite A-listers like Andy Warhol, Norman Mailer, Woody Allen, Mikhail Baryshnikov and many others wined and dined in style for over five decades. Melding historical significance and old world charm with fine modern renovations, this entirely gut-renovated property with newly-restored and updated entrances and common corridors plus all-new finishes throughout exudes a sense of downtown chic complemented by uptown sophistication.
Old world charm is impeccably intertwined with modern style and finishes in this floor-through Two bedroom apartment filled with natural light and character. Both bedrooms have closets, and are generously-sized to accommodate a queen-size bed. The bathroom is lined with beautiful and bright Carrera "hex" mosaic and includes plenty of draw and cabinet storage with three view mirrored medicine cabinets and vanities, as well as authentic white subway tiled shower surrounds and wainscoting. description.81204: The Most Lovely Historical Park Slope GemSituated just blocks away from Prospect Park in one of Brooklyn’s top neighborhoods, this spectacular garden level floor-through apartment boasts front-to-back charm.  The spacious and stately living room features beautifully maintained wood paneling and floors, a decorative fireplace complete with original fleur-de-lis back tiles, and beautiful crown moldings.  Original wallpaper dating to the 1890’s completes the perfect aura. Further back is the brownstone’s original kitchen, featuring the old brick oven (preserved and updated into a handy shelving/storage area), a spacious dining alcove, and loads of built-in cabinets. Top-of-the-line stainless steel appliances have been tastefully incorporated including a dishwasher. The large bathroom opens out into a pleasant sun room and gigantic shared garden patio. So few of the city’s most beautiful homes have retained their original character over the years.  Don’t miss out on a chance to live in one of Park Slope’s finest brownstones and to bask in the undiminished glory of the neighborhood’s renaissance.  Located in prime north Park Slope, you will have Prospect Park, Brooklyn Museum, Brooklyn Botanic Gardens and the Barclays Center within blocks of your home.  5th and 7th Avenues offer myriad dining options as well as boutiques, cafes, bars and amenities of all kinds. description.92382: A truly unique offering, this Historic and Landmarked Single Family Residence combines modern conveniences with post-Civil War Architecture. 312 East 53rd was built in 1866 by Robert and James Cunningham and is one of few remaining wood frame homes in Manhattan. This townhouse features four stories measuring 2,280-square feet, plus a full English basement with walk out to the garden. The garden level with front entry hall, features an updated and very spacious kitchen with stainless steel appliances, granite counter tops and large dining area. The parlor level has a formal entrance from the stoop into a gracious foyer, large living room which extends to a library and half bath adorned with a crystal chandelier. The open staircase brings you up to the third floor with two large bedrooms, one with a separate office. Additionally you will find a large, windowed marble bathroom with double pedestal sink and soaking tub. The entire fourth floor is the master bedroom suite with a dressing room, five closets and a master bath with original tin ceiling. The 1,250-square foot bi-level garden has a slate flagstone patio leading up to the tree-lined garden with planting beds.Other features include a new ductless A/C system, cedar closet, and basement laundry with additional refrigeration.This home is much more than the details in the description. It stands out given the 150 years it has thrived.Bill Harris and Jorg Brockmann published One Thousand New York Buildings and when you come to #318 in the set, you will find, 312 East 53rd. As stated, a reminder that this part of midtown isn't all office towers, only one of these two wood-framed houses has been given Landmark status (#314 has subsequently received landmark designation). But they stand here together as a very rare example of a time when mansard-roofed residences like these could be found in every corner of the city. Looking at the neighborhood that has grown up around them, it is hard to believe that the East 50's was a long haul to the office at one point in time.Notable residences of the home most recently include Zarela Martinez, famed cookbook author and restaurateur, who in 1997 while living in the home, wrote the definitive cookbook The Food and Life of Oaxaca. The home has a rich history of Literaries and Artists alike that resided and also visited the home. Lincoln Kirstein was living at No. 312 and would go on to found the New York City Ballet, he was an author, playwright, art collector and impresario. When Kirstein moved on, No. 312 became the home of Muriel Draper. Draper was renowned as a society hostess whose outgoing, fearless personality shined during this period where she hosted elegant cocktails parties. A lover of the arts who was friends with Gertrude Stein and was social with artists like Henry James and John Singer Sergeant. Kirstein, too, was a close friend of Draper and visited often.

ONE SIXTY MADISON

IMMEDIATE OCCUPANCY - GUARANTOR ACCEPTED

One Sixty Madison, is a newly developed luxury residential tower located in the heart of NoMad, at the nexus of Chelsea, Gramercy and Midtown.

Comprised of 45 stories and 255 market rate studio, one and two bedroom residences, with exteriors by SLCE Architects and interiors by Philip Koether Architects, One Sixty Madison features an angled, octagonal design that enhances the typical New York City street wall.

In addition to its octagon-shaped exterior, One Sixty Madison is positioned at an angle at the corner of Madison Avenue and 33rd street, resulting in unique perspectives allowing for many residences to offer 180 degree city views.

Residences are infused with natural light through floor-to-ceiling windows, while gracious layouts and thoughtful touches emphasize the attention to detail. Layouts offer remarkably furnishable and spacious residences, with many able to accommodate dining tables for up to 6-8 people. Since the early 1990s, the area has been gentrifying, and rents have risen rapidly. Some areas are widely residential and very quiet, while others (especially closer to Roosevelt Avenue) are more urban. Woodside has many of the same good things going for it as its neighbor Sunnyside: low crime, good schools, affordability, and diversity.
